issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field as long and its getter returns long. This creates a cross-artifact type mismatch: students following the specification will implement numberOfLoopings as int (and a getter returning int), while the provided solution and its getter use long. This mismatch can cause confusion and test failures (type/return-value expectations) because the attribute type and accessor signature differ between the specification and the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the type of numberOfLoopings across artifacts. Either: (A) change RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings in the solution (and template) from long to int and make getNumberOfLoopings() return int so it matches the UML/problem statement; or (B) if long is intended, update the problem statement UML and task descriptions to specify numberOfLoopings: long and document that the getter returns long. Option A is recommended to preserve the current UML specification.
